newsitem.title: USA: DeLay-Republicans stick to capital gains position.
newsitem.headline: DeLay-Republicans stick to capital gains position.

text.p: House Republican Whip Tom DeLay said Tuesday that Republicans in Congress were holding to their position that a capital gains tax cut should be broad-based.

"We're going to hold our position, too," DeLay of Texas said. He told a tax conference that it was "very good news" that the Senate Democratic leadership was coming together on capital gains tax proposals.

"It is very good news to have the Democrat leadership -- (Senate Minority Leader Tom) Daschle and (Senate Democratic Whip) Wendell Ford talking in terms of actually coming together on the capital gains proposal," DeLay said.
"I am really looking forward to that and we have to be excited about the fact that maybe we actually will start to do something about the taxes on capital," DeLay said.

While the vote in the Senate on the balanced budget amendment to the Constitution is close, DeLay said "I have no idea what's going to happen in the Senate, but I have a lot of faith in (Senate Majority Leader) Trent Lott's abilities and if he's got the votes he's going to run with it."
DeLay said the votes are there in the House right now to pass the balanced budget amendment. "It's close, but we're doing fine, we've got the votes right now if we can just hold onto them."
